newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends softer, hit by U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends softer, hit by U.S. long bond.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker for the third session in a row on Friday, due mainly to dealers demanding dollars after tracking sharp gains in U.S. long bond yields, tarders said.
"It was a tough market despite the narrow trading range," a dealer said. "Only high secondary interest rates kept the peso from sliding further."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.25 and 2.8 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8350/7.8400 and 7.8320/7.8375 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso slid 5.1 centavos against the dollar over the week.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were down 2-1/4 points in late trade, to yield of 6.47 percent in response to strong manufacturing data.
Same-day peso contracts had closed trade mid-morning 0.4 of a centavo weaker at 7.8040/7.8090 per dollar.
